name: Republic of Iraq

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 435,050 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 434,130 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes the Kurdistan Region.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 47,020,774). Low -1% / high +1.5% for 2026 growth and estimate uncertainty. Includes the Kurdistan Region.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.352 as quoted: 193,000 active (CIA Factbook 2025: ~200,000 under the MoD). Paramilitary 266,000 (IISS) excluded: Popular Mobilization Forces (~200,000, Iran-aligned, partly fighting in the 2026 war) and federal police; KRG Peshmerga (~150,000) also excluded.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: no reserves. High counts the PMF as a callable pool (CIA Factbook ~200,000), not under MoD command.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 193,000 minus infantry P roles (75,000). Covers air force, army aviation, air defence, navy, crews and logistics.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to Iraq's 1980s total-war mobilisation (~1 million of ~17 million, ~6%) scaled down for a volunteer army and divided loyalties (PMF, Peshmerga).

count.note: Educated guess. Iraqi Army infantry/mechanised divisions (14 divisions, many under strength). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces)

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: US/Russian small arms, MRAP mobility.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: Educated guess. Counter-Terrorism Service (~10-15,000) plus light/commando brigades. PMF and Peshmerga excluded. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Armed_Forces)

Equipment list header "Tanks (1325)": M1A1 487, T-90S 210 (SIPRI: 73 delivered), T-72M/Lion of Babylon 478+, T-55 150. The list total is inflated by unserviceable/stored hulls; mid is a judgement of the operational park.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: M1A1M/T-90S modern, T-72M/T-55 old; maintenance weak.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: BMP-3 300 + BMP-1 600 + BTR-4 270 + VN22 200 + BTR-80 100 + M113 500 + MT-LB ~400 + Talha 44 + M1117 324 = ~2,740 listed; Cougar/ILAV MRAPs (1,243) excluded. Serviceability discount gives mid 2,000.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: Listed: SP ~434 (M109 220, AMX-GCT 86, 2S1 90, Type-83 38) + towed ~610 + MRL ~570 (BM-21 300, Type 63 200, Sajil-60 66) = ~1,600; operational share judged ~half.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: IqAF inventory: F-16C/D/IQ 34; low reflects reported serviceability problems after contractor withdrawals. T-50IQ (24) counted as trainers.

Educated guess. Army Aviation: Mi-35M 23 and Mi-28 17 (equipment list), EC725 2, plus Mi-17, Bell 407/IA-407, EC635, Bell 206 without reliable totals. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Air_Force)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: Educated guess. CH-4B MALE drones and ScanEagle. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Air_Force)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: Educated guess. Iraqi Navy patrol ships (Al Basrah, Fatah/Al-Nasr classes) and Swiftships patrol boats around Umm Qasr; Italian-built corvettes/OPVs on order. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraqi_Navy)

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

count.note: Pantsir-S1 24 vehicles (~4 batteries) + MIM-23 Hawk 50 launchers (~8) + Avenger 100 (~8 platoons); KM-SAM ordered 2024 not delivered.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: no long-range SAM; airspace routinely violated (Israel, Turkey, Iran).

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteers, uneven training; CTS elite, regular divisions weaker.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: improved since the 2014 Mosul collapse, but politicised appointments and parallel PMF command.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: sectarian and Kurdish splits; PMF loyalties to Tehran.

weapons.note: Anchor 9 minus: Hellfire, Kornet, some precision bombs; no long-range strike.

armor.note: Anchor 9 minus: M1A1M/T-90S plus older Soviet tanks.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: hardened bases, weak air defence.

isr.note: Anchor 8-9: Cessna ISR, few drones; coalition support reduced.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 458,891,765,241 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 47,020,774 = 9,759 2011 int$. Range +/-12%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 573,256,421,288 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 458,891,765,241 2011 int$. Range +/-12% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 2.45% of GDP in 2025, 1.64% 2022 (low), 3.24% 2019 (high). PMF salaries partly outside the defence budget.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 45.4% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Net importer; Tigris-Euphrates water decline.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 23,613,299 x share of males aged 15-19 10.672% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 504,022. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

roadKm.note: asOf 2025: total 55,100 km (40,362 paved) per the Transport in Iraq article (CIA Factbook figures).

railKm.note: asOf 2014: 2,370 route-km (World Bank); CIA Factbook 2,272 km. Much track damaged since 2014.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 6 ports, 0 large, 1 medium; key ports Al Basrah, Basra Oil Terminal, Khawr al Amaya, Khawr al Zubair, Umm Qasr. Grand Faw port under construction.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: not in the list of flags over 1,000,000 GT, so under ~1.6 million DWT; mid is an educated guess.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys, horses, camels; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Iraq is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar terrain and local supply; population support divided along sectarian lines.

notes: Peacetime-adjacent snapshot: Iraq stayed formally out of the 2026 Iran war but Iran-aligned PMF factions fought (war infobox: PMF casualties April/July 2026) and Gulf states skirmished with them. asOf 2025 economic data, 2026 order of battle. Population and area include the Kurdistan Region (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Ground equipment list totals are inflated by unserviceable vehicles; mids are discounted judgements (grade C). PMF (~200,000) and Peshmerga (~150,000) excluded from forces (they are not under MoD command). Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D).
